_doc: Independent OFFICIAL deterministic-ECDSA known-answer vectors for NIST P-256 and P-384. Each SDK's runtime-vectors test loads this file, reconstructs the compressed public key from (qx,qy) and the raw signature from (r,s), and asserts its native verifyEcdsaP256/P384 ACCEPTS the published signature and REJECTS a 1-bit-tampered one. Values are copied verbatim from RFC 6979 — NOT re-derived from any Runar tier. Verification is signature-source-agnostic: a valid RFC-6979 (r,s) verifies under any correct ECDSA verifier.

_source.spec: RFC 6979 — Deterministic Usage of the Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) and Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA), T. Pornin, August 2013
_source.hash_note: Runar's VerifyECDSAP256 AND VerifyECDSAP384 both hash the message with SHA-256 internally (P-384 codegen uses OP_SHA256, not SHA-384). Therefore BOTH curves use the RFC 6979 'With SHA-256' variant. RFC 6979's bits2int leaves a 256-bit hash unshifted when qlen=384, matching Go/Rust/Python hashToInt — so the same (r,s) verifies.
_source.message_note: message_ascii is the RFC's literal test message ('sample' / 'test'); the native verifier is handed the raw ASCII bytes and hashes them itself.
